ABOUT US

Founded in 2000, McDonald Remodeling is a full-service design/build firm based in Inver Grove Heights, MN, with a dedicated interior design studio and a team that has guided hundreds of Twin Cities homeowners through renovation.

ABOUT US

McDonald Remodeling is about quality design and craftsmanship. These values have been cultivated since Jim McDonald built his first home in 1976. For decades since, we have remodeled homes that are beautiful, enduring, and of the highest quality.

McDonald Remodeling celebrates design down to the last detail. Details make or break a good design and challenging design is our specialty. We relish the chance to dig into our rich knowledge base to come up with a creative and finely crafted transformation for your home.

McDonald Remodeling believes in collaboration. It is key to both good design and great customer service. We design homes that are beautiful and comfortable, striking and practical—homes that fit your unique needs and the time-tested rules of design.

MEET THE TEAM
OUR APPROACH

McDonald Remodeling has honed our remodeling process down to a science. Unlike new construction, remodeling is almost always performed while the homeowners continue to live in the home. Because of this, we consider ourselves a guest in your home, and this fact remains top of mind from the first walk-through to the final clean-up.

Our process, refined over decades, includes precise planning and bidding schedules, personalized project managers, construction superintendents, and close communication with our clients. It is our formula for a smooth remodeling process.

All of this adds up to the final result—a home that is beautiful, enduring, comfortable, and distinctly yours. Perhaps the best testimony to this is the customer comments, awards, and photos below. After reviewing these, we hope you’ll agree that our words ring true.

OUR MISSION STATEMENT

McDonald Remodeling provides high-quality remodeling and design services to homeowners, utilizing an approach rooted in honesty, integrity, creativity and meticulous attention to detail.

We maintain a company culture in which employees are valued and respected. Together, we encourage, support and recognize one another in the delivery of outstanding products and processes. As a result, our services are repeatedly sought after by clients.

PROCESS

McDonald Remodeling uses a structured design/build process that takes Twin Cities homeowners through discovery, design, selections, permitting, construction, and final walkthrough — with one team managing every phase.

MCDONALD REMODELING
PROCESS

Our years of experience enable us to work with our clients in a fluid and thorough process that achieves beautiful, handcrafted custom spaces to make our clients feel even more at home. We design and build for the way you live.

We believe that remodeling your home should be rewarding collaboration from start to finish. So we’ve developed a straight-forward, modern build process, which sets us apart and has proven to deliver projects on time with award-winning results.

The investment of time and diligence during our fine-tuned planning process is essential to keeping goals and timeframes on track during construction. This upfront work really pays dividends once construction begins and allows for a clear plan, organized management, and an enjoyable experience.

McDonald Remodeling’s dedicated team will ensure you have a clear vision of how your remodeling project will unfold to give you the end results you’re looking for.

PROJECT PHASES

DISCOVERY

1-2 weeks approx. time frame

Understanding our clients’ objectives and goals is the first priority of any renovation we embark on. You might be surprised how many people skip this step and design for the sake of design. What you can expect at this point is to have a well-reasoned opinion of what may be possible in your space and an approximate budget that will serve as the road map for the project.

DESIGN

1-2 months approx. time frame

Moving the project into the creative process is usually the most exciting part for our clients and for us. With a solid understanding of how the space needs to function and work for you, we are able to show you a conceptual design of what your new space could look like if you decide you’d like to proceed with a design agreement. With the design comes a detailed proposal outlining all the aspects of your job and a final contract with a fixed price.

REFINEMENT

1-2 months approx. time frame

The design and aesthetics of a space are subjective things. Our initial concepts go through a refinement process where you’ll work with our interior designers to select the elements and materials for your space to make it truly customized to you. For example things like; wood finishes, cabinetry, fixtures, paint color, tile, and flooring are some of the basic elements you might get to consider.

CONSTRUCTION

Time frame depends on project scope and size

After approvals on a finalized design, we set up the construction schedule to ensure your project can be completed in the most efficient way possible. This thorough, planned approach gives McDonald Remodeling the ability to deliver a finished project that meets our high standards of craftsmanship and, most often, exceeds client expectations. 

View fullsize
1.
DISCOVERY
FIRST CONTACT

Thank you for reaching out to us. Whether we’ve spoken on the phone, met at a home show, or exchanged emails with you, we’re glad you decided to get to know us a little better.

HOME VISIT

We kick off with a home visit that informs our team as they work with you to conceptualize the best remodeling options for your space. You’ll have a chance to ask more questions about the benefits and challenges of some ideas you already might be considering.  We’ll also discuss general project and budget estimates.

DESIGN AGREEMENT

If you’re interested in pursuing a project with McDonald Remodeling, the next step is signing a design agreement to proceed with creation of drawings and 3D renderings of your project. Additionally you will be provided a detailed final proposal outlining the work.

View fullsize
2.
DESIGN
CONCEPTUAL DESIGN

We take measurements of your existing home’s floorplan and input it into our 3D software. We’re then able to change the space into different configurations until we find the optimal layout for your home. All this before a hammer or saw has been lifted on your project, helping to shorten the construction time and minimize the disruption a remodeling project can have in your home.

PROPOSAL / SCOPE OF WORK

This document provides deeper discussion of the key components of your project. Additionally, we will review the financial aspect of your project with you which can be more informed by the completed conceptual design.

View fullsize
3.
REFINEMENT
DESIGN/SELECTION MEETINGS

Our initial concepts go through a refinement process until the design has all the elements and materials selected by you with the guidance of our interior designers. For example things like; wood finishes, cabinetry, fixtures, paint color, tile, and flooring are some of the basic elements you might have to consider depending on your remodeling project.

LEARN MORE
View fullsize
4.
CONSTRUCTION
SCHEDULING

Your remodeling project’s tasks and stages will be scheduled down to the day, before your project even begins. This helps ensure that it’s completed in a timely manner eliminating surprises and long delays in getting the work completed.

WORK BEGINS

Throughout your remodeling project, your project manager will help keep you informed and answer any questions you might have as your space is transformed. The work on your home is handled by expert craftspeople in less time with more attention to detail because of our planning process.  You now get to see those 3D drawings come to life.

RENOVATION COMPLETE

Upon completing your project, you’ll take a thorough walk through with your project manager who remains available to answer any questions as you settle back into your space. Now all that’s left is to enjoy!

 LET'S DISCUSS YOUR PROJECT

We’d like to hear more about your remodeling ideas, and we can tell you more about our straightforward approach to achieving your dream space.

GIVING BACK TO THE COMMUNITY

Supporting communities and organizations through giving has always been a cornerstone of our business. We believe a stronger community benefits everyone and doing our part to make the communities we work in and even those thousands of miles away is an important cause we want to contribute to with our time, our talent, and our resources. Every year, our employees give hundreds of hours of volunteer time in their communities and to causes, they are passionate about.

In order to build healthy and safe communities, we work closely with many non-profit organizations that deliver vital services to those that need them. In fact, in the areas of health care, housing, and education our partners have made incredible differences in the lives of thousands of people.

We were honored to partner with Make-A-Wish Minnesota  through NARI Cares to help bring this special boy’s wish to life in Lake Elmo. Henry dreamed of a place in the lower level of his family’s home for his therapy and play equipment. Somewhere he could spend time with his parents and brothers.

Thanks to the generosity of our trade partners, this wish became a reality. A heartfelt thank you to Solid, Above All Flooring, Scherer Bros. Lumber, Kendrick Electric, Binder Heating & Air Conditioning, Riverside Mechanical, Brinka Drywall, Custom One Painting, and Gryphon Tile & Stone for donating their time and expertise.

This project was made possible through the collaboration of our team, our trade partners, and NARI Cares. We are grateful to support Henry and his family and proud to give back to our community!

Founded in 1902, Union Gospel Mission (UGM) is a Christian ministry dedicated to serving people facing homelessness, poverty, or addiction in our community. By meeting physical, spiritual, emotional, and educational needs, the Mission is changing lives! The Mission helps people rebuild their lives by providing safe shelter, nutritious food, medical and dental care, and a broad variety of life-changing programs for children and adults.

Erik’s Ranch & Retreats provides safe and unequaled living, working, social and recreational environments for young adults with autism, using its guiding principles of lifelong learning, individual community building and bidirectional integration through voluntourism.

The Inver Grove Heights BEST Foundation was created to provide scholarships for students graduating from Simley High School. The foundation is separate from, but supportive of, the Inver Grove Heights Community Schools. Learn more.

Wishes & More creates extraordinary experiences for wish children: The goal of this children’s charity is simple: to grant wishes to children with terminal and life-threatening illnesses and provide hopeful hearts, happy memories and assistance to those who love them.

Soldier’s 6 is  a 501(c)3 non profit organization based in Minnesota. They provide honorably discharged veterans, police officers, firefighters, paramedics, correctional officers, and 911 dispatchers with specially trained K-9's. These special dogs will become their Battle Buddy and help guide them through the difficult days in life. 

McDonald Remodeling supports the Simley Band.

McDonald Remodeling supports Farmington Youth Lacrosse.

PAST SUPPORTED ORGANIZATIONS

Second Harvest Heartland works to reinvent hunger relief through leadership and innovation. As the Upper Midwest’s largest hunger relief organization, their goal is not only to help our hungry neighbors today but to provide the means for everyone to be fed tomorrow. In 2011 alone, they collected, warehoused, and distributed more than 70 million pounds of food—but they’re also constantly pioneering ways to reduce waste and better use resources.

The Center for Victims of Torture rebuilds lives and restores the hope of people who survive torture and war atrocities. Through its training of mental health counselors, assistance to torture survivor rehabilitation centers, conducting research, and engaging in public policy and education initiatives CVT aims to put an end to torture. In Minnesota, healing services are provided to torture survivors on an outpatient basis.  Learn more about their work at www.cvt.org

Common Hope promotes hope and opportunity in Guatemala, partnering with children, families, and communities who want to participate in a process of development to improve their lives through education, health care, and housing. 

Learn more about Common Hope

A Christian faith-based non-profit organization that strengthens impoverished communities in Guatemala, partnering with local organizations to improve the quality of life among people through health initiatives such as clean water, basic nutrition, and adequate medical care. They support building projects and ongoing programs in response to the expressed needs of the communities. 

Annual safety camp for kids held every summer. Kids learn how to handle all types of safety issues: fire, water, bike, health and more! Educational sessions will be taught through interactive games and hands on experiences.

McDonald Remodeling has proudly supported the Farmington Youth Hockey Association (FYHA) in their efforts to organize and promote youth hockey for girls and boys with a goal to encourage sportsmanship, teamwork, and individual achievement in hockey.

McDonald Remodeling has proudly supported the Woodbury Girls high school hockey team.

Trying to decide whether to remodel your home or move? Before you start browsing real estate listings or planning a renovation, there are three questions you should ask yourself.

1️⃣ Do you love your location?
If you love your neighborhood, have great schools nearby, or can’t imagine leaving the community you’ve built, it may be worth exploring how your current home could better meet your needs before deciding to move.

2️⃣ Can your home structurally support what you need?
Maybe you’re dreaming of a larger kitchen, more functional storage, an additional bathroom, or more room for your family. It’s time to consider whether your existing home can accommodate those changes and what it would take to make them happen.

3️⃣ Would the cost of moving get you the remodel you want?
Buying a new home comes with more expenses than the purchase price alone. Between moving costs, closing costs, potentially higher monthly payments, and the expense of making a new house feel like home, it’s worth comparing the full cost of relocating with what you could accomplish by investing in your current home.

Of course, there’s no one-size-fits-all answer. The best choice depends on your home, your priorities, your family, and what makes the most sense for your future.

Thinking about selling your home? Before you remodel, it’s worth asking: which improvements will actually matter to a future buyer?

Not every renovation is going to give you the same return, and spending more doesn’t necessarily mean getting more back when it’s time to sell.

Kitchens and bathrooms are often high-impact spaces because buyers notice when they feel dated or don’t function well. Improving curb appeal can also make a difference before a buyer even walks through the front door. But that doesn’t mean you need to completely transform these spaces. Smaller, targeted updates can sometimes make more sense than a full, high-end renovation when your goal is to improve the home before selling.

On the other hand, highly personalized upgrades or major renovations that go far beyond what’s typical for the neighborhood may not recoup their full cost at resale. If an improvement is designed around very specific tastes or adds features that future buyers may not value in the same way, you may not see that investment reflected in the sale price.

The key is knowing what makes sense for your home, your market, and your timeline before you start making decisions.

The right design choices can make a smaller footprint feel open and functional while still giving you plenty of personality. It’s about being intentional with every inch, deciding what you actually need and figuring out what your kitchen actually needs to work well for you.

That might mean skipping upper cabinets to keep the room open. It could mean using shelving for the things you reach for most, incorporating custom cabinetry to maximize storage, or choosing a few standout details that give the kitchen personality without overwhelming the space.

This kitchen in a historic Providence home is a great example of how those choices can work together. The inset cabinetry gives the kitchen a clean, streamlined look without making the cabinetry feel visually heavy. Open shelves provide accessible storage while keeping the walls feeling lighter than a full set of upper cabinets. The overhang on the countertop creates room for bar stools so they can be pushed underneath the counter when they aren’t in use. We want homeowners with smaller kitchens to remember that you don’t need a huge footprint to create a kitchen that feels custom, functional, and completely your own.

Join our award-winning designers on September 19 at 10 AM as they share creative ideas and practical considerations for transforming overlooked spaces throughout your home, from finished basements and home offices to mudrooms and multi-room layouts.

The seminar is complimentary, but seating is limited and pre-registration is required. Have a basement or another underused space you’ve been wondering what to do with? Come get inspired. Register through the link in our bio and join us September 19!

#finishedbasement #basementremodel #designchoices #stressfreeremodel #homerenovations

Think you don’t need an addition? It’s very possible you don’t... but you do need a plan.

When you feel like your home is running out of space, it’s easy to assume the only solution is to build more of it. But before you start thinking about adding square footage, take a look at the spaces you already have.

We’re often quick to write off the spaces that aren’t working for us. The basement becomes the place where everything gets stored. The extra room sits mostly empty. The entryway becomes a pile of shoes, bags, and everything else that doesn’t have a home. But those spaces aren’t necessarily the problem. 

The potential is there. Sometimes it just takes a different way of looking at the space.

This basement is a great example. What started as a dark, overlooked space became a collection of purposeful rooms, including a gym, laundry room, and bathroom. Instead of adding onto the home, the design found new ways for the existing space to work better for the homeowners.

That’s often the first step in transforming an underused space: figuring out what you actually need and then creating a plan to make the space work for you.

That’s what we’ll be exploring at our upcoming seminar, Basements & Multi-Rooms: Transforming Underused Spaces Into Favorite Rooms.

Join our award-winning designers on September 19 at 10 AM as we talk through creative ideas and practical considerations for turning spaces you may have written off into rooms you actually want to use. We’ll be covering finished basements, home offices, mudrooms, and multi-room transformations, along with the planning that makes these spaces work.

The seminar is complimentary, but seating is limited and pre-registration is required.

Before you decide you need to build more, come see what you might be able to do with what you already have. You may walk away seeing a room in your own home a little differently. Register through the link in our bio and join us September 19!

#basementremodel #basementremodeling #basementremodels #finishedbasement #finishedbasements

You’ve finally decided it’s time to remodel. You know which rooms need to change, but how do you make sure it all feels like one home when you’re done?

That’s where a multi-room remodel can get complicated.

You’re not just planning individual spaces. You’re thinking about how they connect, how the design flows from one room to the next, and how all of the pieces work together. There are also the things you may not see in the finished space, like structural changes, plumbing rough-ins, electrical updates, egress requirements, or HVAC extensions.

Every decision can affect something else.

That’s why experience matters so much when you’re remodeling multiple spaces. An experienced design-build team can look at the entire project from the beginning, considering the design, construction, systems, and how your family will actually use each space. That way, we can create a home that feels cohesive and intentional, while still fulfilling your remodel dreams.

This is one of the topics we’ll be discussing at our upcoming seminar, Basements & Multi-Rooms: Transforming Underused Spaces Into Favorite Rooms.

Join our award-winning designers on September 19 at 10 AM as they share creative ideas and practical considerations for transforming underused and connected spaces, from finished basements and home offices to mudrooms and multi-room layouts.

If you’ve been dreaming about changing multiple spaces in your home but aren’t sure where to start, come get inspired. Register through the link in our bio and join us September 19!

#designchoices #stressfreeremodel #homerenovations #designdetails

A well-designed mudroom can change how your whole house feels.

When you have a busy household, the chaos has to go somewhere. And usually, that looks like backpacks landing by the stairs, shoes piling up by the door, jackets ending up on the nearest chair, and somehow, the dog’s leash never being where you thought you left it.

A functional mudroom gives all of those everyday things a place to go.

Think designated zones for each family member. That might mean a drop zone where backpacks and bags can be unloaded as soon as you walk through the door or hooks placed at heights that are reachable for every member of the family. Add a bench with storage underneath for shoes or a dedicated spot for those little things you’re constantly reaching for, like dog treats, and suddenly the room is doing a lot more than storing stuff.

When everything has a designated place, fewer things make their way into the rest of the house. The mudroom functions as a way to contain the chaos of family life. The entryway stays clearer, the kitchen counter stays less cluttered, the dog’s leash is always in the same place, and getting out the door becomes just a little easier.

That’s exactly the kind of thinking we’ll be exploring at our upcoming seminar, Basements & Multi-Rooms: Transforming Underused Spaces Into Favorite Rooms.

Join our award-winning designers on September 19 at 10 AM for creative ideas for making more of the space you already have, including mudrooms, home offices, finished basements, and multi-room transformations.

If your home has a space that could work harder for your family, come get inspired. Register through the link in our bio and join us September 19!

#mudroom #mudroommakeover #mudroomideas #mudroomorganization #mudroomgoals

Does your house have that one room nobody knows what to do with?

Maybe it’s the extra bedroom you don’t really need, or the awkward bonus room, or the space that somehow became a dumping ground for everything without a designated home. Even though you have no idea what to do with them right now, these are all underutilized spaces that are brimming with potential.

All that room needs is a little imagination and some intentional thinking.

Take this space for example. It had the potential to be a lot of things, but when the clients spoke about their lifestyle, it made sense to dedicate the space as a home office. Since both parties needed space to work, his-and-hers workstations made sense to create dedicated spaces to focus, while the generous layout keeps the room feeling open and comfortable.

Underused spaces don’t have to stay that way. In fact, we’ll be talking all about this at our upcoming complimentary seminar, Basements & Multi-Rooms: Transforming Underused Spaces Into Favorite Rooms.

Join our award-winning designers on September 19 at 10 AM as they share creative ideas for turning overlooked spaces into rooms you actually want to use, from home offices and mudrooms to finished basements and multi-room transformations.

Have a room you’re not sure what to do with? Come get inspired. Register through the link in our bio and join us September 19!

#homeoffice #homeofficeideas #homeofficeinterior #homeofficedesign #homeofficegoals

Why should laundry always live in the basement?

If most of your laundry happens upstairs, carrying baskets up and down the stairs can become one of those everyday inconveniences you simply learn to live with. But you don’t necessarily need a huge laundry room to make that routine easier.

A smaller laundry area tucked onto the second floor can put everything right where you need it. A compact washer and dryer can fit into a surprisingly small footprint, and thoughtful additions like a sink for stain treatment or dedicated storage can make the space even more functional.

This kind of setup isn’t just useful for a second-floor laundry area either. A compact laundry unit can be a smart solution for in-law suites or accessory dwelling units, where space is often limited but having everyday conveniences close at hand can make a big difference. Instead of dedicating an entire room to laundry, you can create a functional setup that fits neatly into the space you have while still giving you the independence and convenience of having laundry right where you need it.

That’s exactly the kind of thinking we’ll be exploring at our upcoming seminar, Basements & Multi-Rooms: Transforming Underused Spaces Into Favorite Rooms.

Join our award-winning designers on September 19 at 10 am for creative ideas and practical solutions for making more of the space you already have, whether you’re dreaming about a finished basement, a home office, a mudroom, or a better-functioning multi-room layout.

The seminar is complimentary, but seating is limited and pre-registration is required. Have a space in your home that isn’t being used to its full potential? Come get inspired. Register through the link in our bio and join us September 19!

#laundryroom #laundryroommakeover #laundryroomgoals #laundryroomdesign #laundryroominspo

When you think about the return on investment of a remodel, you probably think about resale value.

And yes, that’s certainly part of it; a thoughtfully designed kitchen or bathroom can add value to your home. But we’d actually argue that the return you’re getting every day is just as important.

Maybe it’s the 10 minutes you get back every morning because your bathroom finally works for your routine. Or maybe it’s not having to dig through three cabinets to find the coffee maker, filters, and coffee beans. Or being able to cook dinner without bumping into everyone else in the kitchen and then sitting down in a space that cultivates conversation. It could even be something as simple as walking into a room that feels calm instead of cluttered.

Those moments don’t have a dollar amount attached to them, but they all have value. Think about how much time a functional layout saves. Thoughtful storage reduces frustration and a space designed around the way you actually live makes everyday life a little easier. 

We’d also be remiss if we didn’t bring up the joy of finally having a home that feels like it’s yours. A remodel allows you to customize the space to be suited to your needs: A kitchen where everyone naturally gathers or a bathroom that feels like a retreat.

Investing in your home doesn’t have to be about maximizing what you’ll get back when you sell. You deserve to enjoy the investment while you live there, too.

If you’ve been hesitating because you’re not sure whether a remodel is “worth it,” maybe the better question is: what would it be worth to you to stop working around your home and start having it work for you? Our designers can help you figure that out. Schedule a complimentary consultation through the link in our bio and let’s talk about what your home could give back to you.

OUR PROCESS

We’re obsessed with every detail in our four-step Design/Build process. Our team of experts will manage every aspect of your project from idea to completion to ensure your remodel exceeds your expectations.

IMAGINE

We start with questions. Why? Because we want to truly understand your lifestyle and how you’ll use your new space. Then, we’ll visit your home to measure and discuss ideas with your budget in mind.

CONCEPTUALIZE

Gain a true picture of the possibilities! Next, we’ll meet in our Design Center to present design concepts with our 3D modeling software to see how your new space could look and feel. We’ll review the scope of work and adjust based upon your needs. Our Project Development Agreement outlines selected concepts and budget, so you can move forward with detailed design and product selections.

COLLABORATE

With your feedback, we’ll transform your concepts into detailed plans and guide you through the myriad of product choices to prepare the roadmap for your new space. We’ll be by your side as you select everything from cabinetry, countertops, to plumbing fixtures, flooring, lighting, accessories and more. Construction documents are finalized and then the fun begins!

BUILD

Let’s make it happen! Our skilled craftspeople are constantly training and updating their skills in all areas including carpentry, plumbing, electrical, flooring and lighting to ensure your project is completed to the highest level of quality and industry standards. You’ll be introduced to your installation team and they’ll review every detail of the buildout with you before construction even begins. All materials are ordered, received, and inspected at our facility and then our team is ready to install. Your satisfaction is always guaranteed, and we’ll will treat your home with the utmost care, always maintaining a clean and orderly worksite.

ABOUT US

As a family-owned, full-service Design Build residential remodeler, we are renowned for our nationally award-winning work in kitchens, baths, mudrooms, pantries, built-ins, multi-room renovations, game rooms, bar areas, and more.

We specialize in creating spaces that cater to various life stages, from raising families and entertaining friends to providing for loved ones or facilitating aging in place. We take pride in meeting our clients exactly where they are in life. We find immense joy in our direct impact on people’s lives as they welcome us into their homes and trust us to uphold our promises.

Recognized as one of the Best Places to Work in RI by Providence Business News from 2018 to 2024 and the only Rhode Island contractor on the Remodeling 550 list (honoring America’s largest remodelers), we have earned a reputation for quality craftsmanship and exceptional style. We are fully committed to customer satisfaction.

We invite you to explore our expansive 3,000-square-foot showroom at 139 Jefferson Boulevard, Warwick, RI. Discover full-size displays of the latest trends in appliances, countertops, cabinetry hardware, tile, plumbing, lighting, and more. Don’t miss our complimentary remodeling seminars, designed to inspire with new product innovations, styles, and trends.

Our Story

Since we opened our doors in 1989, we have earned a reputation as the leading Rhode Island kitchen and bathroom remodeling company. Our Design+Build approach gives us a distinct advantage over other general contractors. Where other companies only offer limited services, we take a complete approach to every job, overseeing the planning, designing, and installation of every project. This gives us better control over scheduling, quality and costs, and results in a project that is completed with fewer delays and – a very important consideration – less stress for our customers!

A Little History

From the very beginning, we have an emphasis on hiring talented people with a passion for remodeling and designing, and a desire to please customers. Over the years, we have built a team of professionals who are among the most skilled and experienced in the industry. We continue to emphasize training and skill building, and several of our Design Consultants have become Certified Kitchen & Bath (CKD) designers as well as Certified Aging in Place Specialists (CAPS). We have also been certified by the EPA as a LeadSafe contractor. Our passion for professionalism and commitment to customer satisfaction has led the company to be the leading design/build company in the area.

An Unparalleled Guarantee

We are so confident in our work that every project is guaranteed for a full five years with our Quality Assurance and Five-Year Workmanship Warranty. This is on top of the manufacturer warranties that accompany many of the products we install. No remodeling company can deliver the peace of mind that comes with such a strong guarantee.

Given their professionalism and quality of work, I would not hesitate to recommend RIKB to anyone anticipating a home remodeling project of whatever size or scope.” -Mike

“RIKB did a complete remodel of my kitchen and each and every person I worked with was exceptional from the design to the completion of the project. The crew was professional and knowledgeable about details and went above and beyond in the quality of their work. They said the project would be complete in three and a half weeks and as skeptical as I was they were finished in the scheduled time frame. RIKB you are an exceptional team!”

COMMUNITY SERVICE

At RIKB, corporate social responsibility is part of our DNA. From our employees, to partners, to clients and potential clients, we encourage everyone to give back. Whether through their time, contributions, or donating used building materials, here are a few of the organizations we support.

Potter League for Animals

The Potter League for Animals is Rhode Island’s go-to animal care and resource center, where we provide shelter, veterinary care, behavior training, spay & neuter, owner assistance programs, humane education, and the opportunity for thousands of animals to find loving homes each year.

Visit Site
Habitat for Humanity ReSTORES

ReStore is a non-profit home improvement store and donation center that sells new and gently used furniture, building materials, appliances and home accessories to the public at a fraction of the retail price. With help from local donors, shoppers and volunteers, proceeds from ReStore sales are used to build homes in South County and around the world!

Visit Site
EcoBuilding Bargains

EcoBuilding Bargains is the largest used building materials store in New England offering deals on re-used and surplus materials, including cabinets, architectural salvage, lumber, doors, windows, tile, appliances, lighting fixtures, and furniture. Their mission is to help New England home owners stay green by keeping thousands of tons of useful materials out of landfills. EcoBuilding Bargains accepts donations of quality, but unwanted, home improvement materials and sells them to the public at low prices in a convenient retail setting.

Visit Site
Rhode Island Community Food Bank

Since 1982, the Rhode Island Community Food Bank has been distributing millions of pounds of food to those in need of assistance through our network of member agencies across the state. We love sup-porting this organization and assisting our neighbors across Rhode Island. At all of the seminars we host throughout the year, accept food donations from attendees and are proud to provide monetary do-nations on behalf our of clients throughout the year.

Visit Site
Toys for Tots

The U. S. Marine Corps Reserve Toys for Tots Program collects new, unwrapped toys during October, November and December each year, and distribute those toys as Christmas gifts to less fortunate children in the community. We agree that every child deserves a little Christmas. That’s why, year after year, our design center is always on the list of drop off locations.
